hook.text: The genome was divided among 20 labs in 6 countries. Each lab sequenced a chunk. Trust held it together.

buildup.text: Labs in the U.S., UK, France, Germany, Japan, and China split chromosomes. It was a genomic assembly line.

discovery.text: The Wellcome Trust Sanger Centre in the UK sequenced one-third alone—the single biggest contribution.

twist.text: All data was released publicly within 24 hours of generation. No patents. No secrets. Open science won.

climax.text: The Bermuda Principles required immediate data release. This decision shaped open science for a generation.

punchline.text: Six countries agreed on one thing: the genome belongs to everyone.

quiz.question: What did the Bermuda Principles require?
